annotation.title_clean: FROM ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TO ARTIFICIAL CONSCIOUSNESS: POSSIBLE LEGAL BASES FOR THE HUMAN-ROBOT RELATIONSHIPS IN THE FUTURE
annotation.title_en: FROM ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TO ARTIFICIAL CONSCIOUSNESS: POSSIBLE LEGAL BASES FOR THE HUMAN-ROBOT RELATIONSHIPS IN THE FUTURE
annotation.summary_en: Conceptual article distinguishing artificial intelligence from artificial consciousness and exploring the future legal status of social robots. It reviews the current EU legal position on AI, especially copyright and database protection, and considers scenarios such as robots as property or slaves versus equality-based legal status.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robots are currently treated as property; future conscious robots may demand rights.
Applying Roman slave law to robots is anthropocentric and unsustainable long-term.
Equality-based legal solutions are more reasonable for human-robot relations.
Copyright under EU law protects only human creative activity; AI output is not a work.
Law must change rapidly to address responsibility for non-rational decisions of conscious machines.
